Compute the joint site frequency spectrum of all populations

Source: R/nwise_pop_sfs.R
nwise_pop_sfs.Rd

Compute the multidimensional (joint) site frequency spectrum (SFS) of all the populations of a grouped gen_tibble, i.e. the number of loci with each combination of numbers of copies of the derived (or minor) allele in the populations (the "multiSFS" of easySFS and fastsimcoal2). Missing genotypes are dealt with as in easySFS, by projecting each population down to n_proj allele copies (see pop_sfs() for details). Only the loci with at least n_proj called allele copies in every population are used. A folded spectrum is folded on the total number of copies across all populations (as in dadi).

Usage

nwise_pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
nwise_pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  max_cells = 1e+07,
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(.x), 1),
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

a grouped gen_tibble (as obtained by using dplyr::group_by()), with at least two groups.

...

other arguments passed to specific methods, currently unused.

n_proj

the number of allele copies to project each population to: either a single value used for all populations, a vector with one value per population (in the order of the groups), or a vector named with the group labels. If NULL (the default), each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (see pop_sfs_preview()).

folded

boolean, whether to fold the spectrum (the default, as the ancestral allele is not usually known). If FALSE, the spectrum is polarised with ancestral.

ancestral

the ancestral allele of each locus, used to polarise unfolded spectra: either the name of a column of the loci table (see show_loci()), or a character vector with one allele per locus (in the order of the loci table). Loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their alleles are dropped. If NULL (the default), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS. Ignored, with a warning, for folded spectra.

type

the type of object to return, either "tidy" (the default) or "array".

fastest

the order of the cells in the tidy output: "last" (the default) keeps the order of the populations, so that the rows are sorted by the number of allele copies in the first population, then in the second, and so on (the number of copies in the last population changes fastest, as in the files written by dadi and easySFS); "first" makes the number of copies in the first population change fastest.

max_cells

the maximum number of cells of the spectrum; an error is raised for larger spectra, to avoid running out of memory.

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

block_size

maximum number of loci read at once.

Value

If type = "tidy", a tibble with one row per cell of the joint spectrum, with one column per population (named with the group labels) giving its number of copies of the derived (or minor) allele (see allele_count in pop_sfs()), n_sites (the projected number of sites) and masked (whether the cell is masked, see pop_sfs()). The projection of each population is stored in the attribute n_proj. If type = "array", an sfs object (see pop_sfs()), an array with one dimension per population.

Details

Populations are in the order of the groups (see dplyr::group_keys()): to change their order (which matters for dadi and fastsimcoal2), change the order of the levels of the grouping variable (e.g. with factor()); to use a subset of the populations, filter() the gen_tibble (empty groups are dropped). The spectrum has prod(n_proj + 1) cells, which grows quickly with the number of populations.

See also

pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs(), pop_sfs_preview()

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

example_gt %>% nwise_pop_sfs(n_proj = 2)
#> # A tibble: 27 × 5
#>     pop1  pop2  pop3 n_sites masked
#>    <int> <int> <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#>  1     0     0     0  0.617  TRUE  
#>  2     0     0     1  0.967  FALSE 
#>  3     0     0     2  0.200  FALSE 
#>  4     0     1     0  0.117  FALSE 
#>  5     0     1     1  0.533  FALSE 
#>  6     0     1     2  0.142  FALSE 
#>  7     0     2     0  0.0333 FALSE 
#>  8     0     2     1  0.15   FALSE 
#>  9     0     2     2  0      TRUE  
#> 10     1     0     0  0.6    FALSE 
#> # ℹ 17 more rows

# the first population changing fastest
example_gt %>% nwise_pop_sfs(n_proj = 2, fastest = "first")
#> # A tibble: 27 × 5
#>     pop1  pop2  pop3 n_sites masked
#>    <int> <int> <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#>  1     0     0     0  0.617  TRUE  
#>  2     1     0     0  0.6    FALSE 
#>  3     2     0     0  0.283  FALSE 
#>  4     0     1     0  0.117  FALSE 
#>  5     1     1     0  0.6    FALSE 
#>  6     2     1     0  0.142  FALSE 
#>  7     0     2     0  0.0333 FALSE 
#>  8     1     2     0  0.133  FALSE 
#>  9     2     2     0  0      TRUE  
#> 10     0     0     1  0.967  FALSE 
#> # ℹ 17 more rows
